samples_reviewed.question_text: Write one third in fraction notation.
hints: A fraction shows how many equal parts are shaded out of the total.
The denominator (bottom number) tells the total equal parts: 3.
The numerator (top number) tells how many parts are taken: 1.
So the fraction is 1/3.

clause_evidence.reasoning: Nine samples directly test reading competency: six ask students to identify the word name of a displayed fraction (samples 3, 6, 7, 8, 9, 11, 13, 14, 16). These samples range across halves, thirds, fourths, fifths, sixths, and eighths, ensuring that reading is taught and practiced across the unit fraction denominator space. The reading direction is explicit in all cases, and word names are requested in age-appropriate language.

Ten samples directly test writing competency: students convert word names to fraction notation (samples 1, 2, 4, 5, 10, 12, 15, 17, 18, 19). These samples span halves, thirds, fourths, fifths, sixths, and eighths, ensuring writing is practiced across multiple denominators. Samples are presented in both cloze and multiple-choice formats, with one-eighth and one-third each appearing multiple times to support automaticity.

All 19 samples use unit fractions exclusively, with numerator always equal to 1 and denominators ranging from 2 to 8. No sample introduces fractions with numerators greater than 1, non-unit fractions, or any concept beyond unit fraction identification and naming. The consistent restriction to numerator 1 ensures students learn only the competency-specified subset of fractions.

All samples reference or require fraction notation in at least one modality. Reading samples display fractions using LaTeX formatting such as \(\frac{1}{2}\) or plain text like 1/3. Writing samples expect students to produce notation forms. Hints explain numerator and denominator roles. Both notation types (symbolic fraction form and corresponding word names) are consistently represented across the sample set.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: Grade 2 Quarter 4 students are developmentally ready for identifying and naming simple unit fractions. The problem complexity—naming or writing 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 1/6, 1/8—matches quarter 4 expectations. No multi-step operations, no fractions with numerators greater than one, and straightforward terminology are all appropriate cognitive scaffolds for this grade level.

competency_alignment.rationale: All 19 samples directly address the competency verb pair of reading and writing unit fractions. Reading samples ask for word names when shown fraction notation; writing samples ask for notation when given word names. The content consistently targets only unit fractions (numerator always 1) and uses authentic fraction notation without scope creep into concepts like equivalence, comparison, or operations.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The decomposition into read, write, unit fractions, and fraction notation is lossless and captures all binding aspects of the competency. Reading and writing represent the full spectrum of the competency verb pair. Unit fractions precisely scope the domain to numerator 1. Fraction notation covers both written form (1/3, 1/4) and word form requirements.

decomposition.reasoning: The four requirements cleanly decompose the competency without loss. The read/write boundary partitions the bidirectional nature of the competency. Unit fractions and fraction notation bind the mathematical objects and representation forms. No aspect of the printed competency statement remains unaddressed by this decomposition.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: The sample set covers denominators 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8, providing breadth across common unit fractions taught in grade 2. Both reading (nine samples) and writing (ten samples) are well represented. Presentation modes include direct fraction stems with LaTeX notation, word-based denominators, and thematic wrappers. Question formats span cloze and multiple-choice, with options that test common misconceptions like inverted fractions and non-unit distractors.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All samples maintain uniform cognitive difficulty appropriate to grade 2 quarter 4 baseline expectations. There is no attempted difficulty gradient within this node, which is appropriate because unit fraction literacy at this stage is a foundational skill requiring consolidation before progression. Variations in denominator value (2 through 8) provide practice breadth without escalating cognitive demand.

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The generator produces meaningful variants across multiple dimensions: numerator/denominator selection varies the unit fraction value, question type alternates between reading and writing, presentation format shifts between direct notation and word description, and experience level is differentiated (standard, hint_gated, mastery_drill, scaffolded). Thematic variation through emoji and object wrappers adds engagement without complicating the mathematical task.
